subject: maths
title: Coordinates & Quadrants
welcome_lead: Every point on a graph has an address. Learn to plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants.
meta_desc: Master coordinates and the four quadrants in this KS3 graphs adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! Coordinates are now second nature.

concepts.def: Pair of numbers (x, y) locating a point.
One of four regions on a coordinate grid.
Coordinates written (x, y) in this order.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Start at origin (0, 0). Move 3 right along the x-axis.

Then move 2 up along the y-axis. Mark the point.

Quadrant 1: x > 0, y > 0 (top right).
Quadrant 2: x < 0, y > 0 (top left).
Quadrant 3: x < 0, y < 0 (bottom left).
Quadrant 4: x > 0, y < 0 (bottom right).

For (-2, 3): move 2 left from origin, then 3 up.

This lands in Quadrant 2.

mcqs.q: How do you use a conversion graph between miles and kilometres?
options: Pick any point on the line — they're all equivalent.
The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.
Look only at the gradient of the line and apply it as a formula.
Find the known value on its axis, draw a line to the graph, then read across (or down) to the other axis.

mcqs.q: In the equation y = 3x + 5, what does the 5 represent on the graph?
options: The y-intercept — the value of y when x = 0 (where the line crosses the y-axis).
The gradient — how steep the line is.
Pick any point on the line — they're all equivalent.
The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.

mcqs.q: What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
How long the line is on the page.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.
Pick any point on the line — they're all equivalent.
